_how: Friday 'From the website' posts (when no feast is coming) go down this list in order and don't repeat a feature until all have been shown. Each shot is a real screenshot of orthodoxdaily.net taken nightly on GitHub by scripts/site_shots.py following its recipe; if a recipe can't be followed (e.g. no livestream today) the last good screenshot is kept. 'about' is the fact sheet the caption is written from. Edit, add or reorder freely.

features.title: Today’s readings, your way
features.line: Every reading of the day, with text you can make larger for comfort.
features.about: On the Home page, the Scripture card lists the day's readings. Tapping one opens the full passage in a window with − and + buttons that make the text smaller or larger (90% to 150%).

shots.heading: Make the text larger
shots.text: Open any reading and use the − and + buttons for a comfortable size.

steps: Open orthodoxdaily.net
In the Scripture card, tap a reading
Use − and + to change the text size

features.title: A short guide to the readings
features.line: An AI reading guide that explains the day’s Scripture from an Orthodox perspective.
features.about: In a reading's window, the sparkles button opens the 'Orthodox AI reading guide': a short explanation of the passage written by AI from an Orthodox perspective. It is a help for understanding, not a teaching of the Church.

shots.heading: Tap the sparkles
shots.text: A short, plain explanation of the passage, written by AI from an Orthodox perspective.

steps: Open a reading from the Scripture card
Tap the sparkles button at the top
Read the short guide under the passage

features.title: The readings, inside your prayers
features.line: Morning and Evening Prayers bring the day’s readings to you, right where you pray.
features.about: The Morning Prayers page includes the day's Epistle and Gospel; the Evening Prayers page includes the Vespers readings, with a reminder of the Epistle and Gospel if you missed them.

shots.heading: Read them as you pray
shots.text: Morning has the Epistle and Gospel; Evening has the Vespers readings.

steps: Open Morning or Evening in the menu
Scroll to the readings section
Tap a reading to open it

features.title: Pray along out loud
features.line: Listen to the prayers and the psalm of the day while you pray.
features.about: On the Morning and Evening Prayers pages, the headphones button opens an audio player for the prayers, and the 'Play Psalm' button plays the psalm of the day.

shots.heading: Tap the headphones
shots.text: An audio player for the prayers, and a button to hear the psalm of the day.

steps: Open Morning or Evening in the menu
Tap the headphones next to the title
Or tap Play Psalm to hear the psalm

features.title: Pray before the icons
features.line: Open the icons of Christ and the Mother of God beside your prayers.
features.about: On the Morning and Evening Prayers pages, the Icons button shows the icons of the Mother of God and of Christ side by side, to pray before.

shots.heading: Tap Icons
shots.text: The Mother of God and Christ, side by side, above your prayers.

steps: Open Morning or Evening in the menu
Tap Icons near the top
Tap it again to hide them

features.title: A psalm for each day
features.line: Every morning and evening, the prayers include the psalm appointed for that day of the week.
features.about: The Morning and Evening Prayers each include a 'Psalm of the Day' that changes with the day of the week (for example, Sunday morning Psalm 5, Sunday evening Psalm 69).

shots.heading: Psalm of the Day
shots.text: A different psalm for each day of the week, morning and evening.

steps: Open Morning or Evening in the menu
Scroll to Psalm of the Day
Come back tomorrow for the next one

features.title: The Church year at a glance
features.line: Browse month by month, with feast days highlighted in blue.
features.about: The Calendar page shows a month at a time; the arrows move through the year. Feast days are shaded light blue, and tapping any day shows its feast, saints, fasting and readings.

shots.heading: Month by month
shots.text: Feast days are shaded blue. Tap any day for its saints, fasting and readings.

steps: Tap Calendar in the menu
Use the arrows to change month
Tap a day to see everything about it

features.title: Know the fast for every day
features.line: Coloured dots on the calendar show the fasting rule for each day.
features.about: On the Calendar page each fasting day has a coloured dot. The Calendar Legend explains them: blue for fish, wine and oil allowed; purple for wine and oil allowed; amber for meat fast only; grey for a strict or other fast. Feast days are shaded light blue.

shots.heading: Read the dots
shots.text: Open the legend to see what each colour means.

steps: Tap Calendar in the menu
Tap View legend
Tap a day for its fasting rule

features.title: Meet the day’s saints
features.line: Read the life of each saint of the day, often with their icon.
features.about: Each saint commemorated on a day has an 'About' button (on the Calendar) or link (on Home) that opens their life. When a matching, freely licensed icon is found, it is shown beside the life and can be opened full screen.

shots.heading: Tap About
shots.text: The saint’s life, and their icon when one is available.

steps: Tap Calendar in the menu
Under Commemorations, tap About
Tap the icon to see it full screen

features.title: Understand the feast
features.line: On feast days, a short AI reflection explains what the Church celebrates.
features.about: On feast days, the Feast card has a sparkles button that opens a short 'Feast day AI insight' written for newcomers. It is a help for understanding, not a teaching of the Church.

shots.heading: Tap the sparkles on a feast
shots.text: A short reflection on the feast, written by AI for newcomers.

steps: Tap Calendar in the menu
Tap a blue (feast) day
Tap the sparkles on the Feast card

features.title: Prepare for Confession, gently
features.line: A guided examination of conscience, woven into the prayers before Confession.
features.about: The Confession page has four steps: an opening prayer, an examination (tap the items that apply from three lists), prayers that include what you selected, and a confession draft to read before the priest, with a short guide on how to confess.

shots.heading: Tap what applies
shots.text: Three short lists help you examine your conscience.

steps: Tap Confession in the menu
Go through the four steps
Read the draft before the priest

features.title: Your confession stays yours
features.line: What you select is woven into the prayers and a draft to read before the priest, and never leaves your phone.
features.about: On the Confession page, the items you tap are inserted into the prayers ('I confess that I have:') and into a final draft to read before the priest. They exist only on the open page: nothing is saved or sent anywhere, and everything is gone when you leave the page.

shots.heading: A draft for Confession
shots.text: Only on your screen: nothing is saved or sent, and it’s gone when you leave.

steps: Tap Confession in the menu
Tap what applies in the Examination
Open the Confession Draft

features.title: Your calendar, your tradition
features.line: Choose New or Old Calendar, Slavic or Greek, and your Bible translation.
features.about: The Settings (gear) button lets you choose New or Old Calendar, Slavic or Greek tradition, and the Scripture translation (LXX2012 & WEB, or King James). Your choices are saved on your device.

shots.heading: Tap the gear
shots.text: Your choices are saved on this device.

steps: Tap the gear at the top
Pick your calendar, tradition and translation
They’re remembered next time

features.title: Easy on the eyes at night
features.line: Dark mode for evening prayers, and seasonal touches through the year.
features.about: The moon button switches the site to dark mode (and the sun back to light). The leaf button turns on gentle seasonal effects: snow in winter, rose petals in spring, sun rays in summer and falling leaves in autumn.

shots.heading: Tap the moon
shots.text: A dark version of every page, for evening prayer.

shots.heading: Tap the leaf
shots.text: Snow, rose petals, sun rays or falling leaves, depending on the season.

steps: Tap the moon at the top for dark mode
Tap the leaf for seasonal effects
Both are remembered next time

features.title: Sunday Liturgy, live
features.line: On Sundays and feast days, watch the Divine Liturgy live from Orthodox parishes.
features.about: On Sundays and feast days, a livestream card on Home shows the Divine Liturgy from one of four parishes (Pittsburgh, St. Mary's Minneapolis, St. Anne, Hawaii), live, upcoming or as today's recording. You can switch parish, and it plays right on the page.

shots.heading: Watch from home
shots.text: Choose a parish and press play, right on the page.

steps: Open orthodoxdaily.net on a Sunday or feast day
Find the livestream card on Home
Pick a parish and press play
